• Scientific name: Malapterurus minjiriya Sagua, 1987
  • Type locality: Lake Kainji, lower Niger River basin, Nigeria
  • IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated
Africa: known from the Niger River and Volta River system, the White Nile (Barro and Alvero Rivers) and the Omo River; probably also in the Chad and Senegal basins but has not been collected there.
Unreported in the aquarium. There is no breeding report.

Identification: body with moderately to very large black spots irregularly scattered. Compared to M. electricus, its oral tooth bands are much larger.

Etymology: Malapterurus comes from the Greek malakos, meaning soft, pteron, meaning fin, and oura, meaning tail; presumably in reference to the adipose fin, which appears all the more prominent in the absence of the rayed dorsal fin.
Journal of Fish Biology v. 30 (no. 1), pp 78, Fig. 1.
